chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi and Jamil and Hisham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The proof is upon the one who claims, and the oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made.'

key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: The proof or evidence presented by the claimant
key_terms.الْيَمِينُ: The oath taken by the defendant
key_terms.مَنِ ادَّعَى: The one who makes the claim
key_terms.مَنِ ادُّعِيَ عَلَيْهِ: The one against whom the claim is made

ai.seo_question: What is the rule of burden of proof in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of al-Tusi's Tahdhib, codifies the principle of 'al-bayyinah 'ala man i'dda' (proof is upon the claimant), which serves as the foundational rule for civil litigation in Shia jurisprudence. It establishes that the burden of proof rests on the plaintiff, while the defendant may secure their position through an oath if the plaintiff fails to provide sufficient evidence, a mechanism deeply rooted in the Prophetic tradition and elaborated upon by scholars like al-Shaykh al-Tusi in the context of judicial procedure.
